questions.key_step: Nearest point means the join is normal to the curve, giving $\alpha\beta=\frac{9}{2}$ with $\beta^2=6\alpha$.
questions.justification: Single known move (normal through the point) then a short algebraic solve; numerical answer with no options adds a little precision risk. Comparable to the routine tangent-angle question 2026-P2-Q17 (L2).

questions.key_step: Solve $f'>0$ piece by piece: $(0,\frac{3}{2})$ from the cubic and $(-1,0]$ from $3e^x(1+x)$.
questions.justification: Two routine sign-of-derivative inequalities joined together; option checking is easy. Similar in weight to 2021-P2-Q10 (L2) and below 2026-P1-Q1 (L3), which needs an auxiliary function.

questions.key_step: Factor $f'$ as $6\sin x\cos x(2\sin x+1)(\sin x+2)$ and read the sign on the domain.
questions.justification: Differentiate, factor a quadratic in $\sin x$, read a sign chart; three routine stages with no insight. Matches the routine-chain definition of Level 2 and sits below 2026-P1-Q1 (L3).

questions.key_step: Build $A$ correctly from the rule, get $f=4x^3-4x^2-4x$, and add the local extremum values.
questions.justification: Determinant expansion, derivative, two evaluations: a routine chain of standard steps with options to check. Slightly wordy question (global vs local). Comparable to 2021-P2-Q10 (L2).

questions.key_step: Increasing then decreasing at $\frac{3}{4}$ forces $f'\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)=0$, so $a=-4$ (negative).
questions.justification: One standard move (turning point gives $f'=0$) followed by a one-line sign check on a quadratic; no chaining. Matches Level 1 'one familiar move' such as 2024-P2-Q3 (L1).

questions.key_step: Treat $f''(1),f''(2)$ as constants; differentiate twice to evaluate them, then find the local minimum.
questions.justification: Self-referential constants are a small twist, then a standard cubic extremum; three routine stages. Level 2 as in 2021-P2-Q10-type local extrema computations.

questions.key_step: Spot $(q^3-1)^2$ and the homogeneous quadratic $p^2-pq-12q^2=(p-4q)(p+3q)$, then count roots of two cubics.
questions.justification: The key regrouping into a hidden quadratic is not a routine drill; afterwards two monotonicity/root-counting checks. Idea availability is moderate and it is option-based. Placed one level above the routine chain, near 2026-P1-Q1 (L3).

questions.key_step: Write the rectangle's height as a linear function of its base to get $A=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}l(2\sqrt2-l)$.
questions.justification: Standard optimisation set-up (geometry to one variable) then a quadratic maximum; numerical answer. Several routine steps, no insight needed. Level 2, comparable to 2026-P2-Q17 (L2).

questions.key_step: Eliminate to get $x_1^2=\frac{a^2b}{a+b}$, $y_1^2=\frac{ab^2}{a+b}$ and the angle formula collapses to $\frac{a-b}{\sqrt{ab}}$.
questions.justification: Standard angle-between-curves method but heavy symbolic algebra with $a,b$; one slip leads to a wrong option, although options help. Level 3, one above routine, near 2026-P2-Q17 (L2) but with more algebra.

questions.key_step: Common point $\left(\frac{3}{2},\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)$, then $m_1=-\frac{1}{3\sqrt3}$, $m_2=-\sqrt3$ in the angle formula.
questions.justification: Intersection point, two tangent slopes and the angle formula: a routine chain of standard steps with options to check. Matches 2026-P2-Q17 (angle between tangents of two ellipses, L2).

questions.key_step: Rearrange to $e^{3x}=1+\frac{4}{e^x+2}$ and compare monotonic behaviour.
questions.justification: Single move: rearrange so one side increases and the other decreases, then check existence. A few routine steps in the style of 2024-P2-Q10 (L1, zeros of an increasing function), but the rearrangement is less direct, so one level up.

questions.key_step: Subtract the line to get three zeros, then apply Rolle twice.
questions.justification: One familiar idea (Rolle applied repeatedly) with a quick option check; no heavy computation. Similar in nature to the Rolle/IVT reasoning of 2021-P2-Q3 (L2) but shorter and with options.

questions.key_step: Spot $x_4=2+\frac{2}{\sqrt3}$ as the only critical point and test both statements.
questions.justification: Two statements, each needing a genuine check, with a short computation for each and no option elimination. Placed at 3 in line with 2026-P1-Q1 (L3, sign of f' and extrema); the routine algebra keeps it at the lower end of Advanced.

questions.key_step: Evaluate $f$ at its three critical points and read off sign changes.
questions.justification: Routine chain: factor $f'$, test signs, evaluate three values; numerical answer with no options to check against. Close to 2024-P2-Q10 (L1) and 2021-P1-Q17 (L1) in idea, but with more evaluations, so L2.

questions.key_step: Convert the monotonic condition into $a\ge-2x$ for all $x\in[1,2]$ and use the extreme value.
questions.justification: A single standard idea (sign of $f'$ on an interval, extreme endpoint) applied twice. Like 2024-P2-Q10 (L1) in demand; answer is a number but the computation is trivial.

questions.key_step: Logarithmic differentiation, then $2\ln2-1=\ln\frac4e$ makes the critical point clean.
questions.justification: Routine chain: log, differentiate, simplify, sign check, evaluate; the algebra with $\ln 2$ and $e$ needs care but options help. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q9 (L2, routine chain then maximum).

questions.key_step: Write the total area in one variable and solve $\frac{dA}{dx}=0$.
questions.justification: Several routine steps (areas of regular figures, one-variable setup, derivative, algebra with surds) but no insight; options let the student check the surd form. Level 2 like other routine chains (2023-P2-Q9).

questions.key_step: Volume $=(a-2x)(b-2x)x$; take the smaller root of $V'=0$.
questions.justification: Standard textbook optimisation: one setup, one quadratic derivative, pick the smaller root. One familiar move, similar to 2024-P2-Q10 (L1) in demand.

questions.key_step: Let $k=x$ be the circle's length; the stationarity equation gives $\left(\frac4\pi+1\right)x$ directly.
questions.justification: Standard setup and a one-line derivative; the only twist is recognising that the requested expression equals the left side of the stationarity equation. Numerical format, so one level above plain option-based optimisation.

questions.key_step: Translate the conditions to $f''(-1)=0$ and $f'(1)=0$ and integrate $f''=a(x+1)$ twice.
questions.justification: Decode two conditions into $f''(-1)=0$ and $f'(1)=0$, then solve a small linear system: routine chain of several standard steps with no options. Similar to 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).

questions.key_step: S=4*pi*r^2 with dS/dt constant makes r^2 linear in t.
questions.justification: One familiar related-rates setup solved by a single integration; matches the single-move Level 1 pattern. Slightly easier than the separable DEs of 2025-P1-Q13 (L2).

questions.key_step: Tangent slope equals slope of OP, giving 2a^3+3a^2-5=0.
questions.justification: Standard tangent-through-a-point setup with an obvious root, then option testing. One familiar move, like 2024-P2-Q10 (L1).

questions.key_step: Similar triangles h=5r, then S=sqrt26*pi*r^2 and chain rule.
questions.justification: Routine chain of several standard steps (similarity, volume, slant area, chain rule) with no insight needed, so Level 2 as for 2026-P2-Q3.

questions.key_step: dy/dx=(1+sin t)/cos t, then solve 1+sin t=sqrt3 cos t.
questions.justification: Parametric slope simplifies cleanly and the trig equation is a standard auxiliary-angle move; one familiar idea chain, Level 1.

questions.key_step: Slope at (a,b) is -b/a for every n, so the line is always the tangent.
questions.justification: A single implicit differentiation shows the claim for all n; direct, no counting or casework.

questions.key_step: Differentiate constraint and volume w.r.t. r and eliminate dx/dr.
questions.justification: Routine constrained optimisation with surface-area bookkeeping and long arithmetic but no insight; options help. Level 2 like 2026-P2-Q8.

questions.key_step: Normal through Q gives 4h^3+3h^2-3h-4=0 with root h=1.
questions.justification: Several routine steps ending in a cubic whose rational root must be spotted, no options to check; a numerical format nudges it to 2-3. Easier than 2024-P2-Q12 (L4).

questions.key_step: Single maximum at x=2 with f to -infinity at both ends decides all four statements.
questions.justification: Four statements each needing a genuine check (sign analysis, root counting, numeric evaluation of f'(e) and f(e)), as in 2026-P1-Q1 (L3) but in an option-based format.

questions.key_step: Extremum values f(-1)=4>0 and f(1)=-8<0 give three roots.
questions.justification: A standard root-counting-by-extrema trick applied once; single familiar move.

questions.key_step: f'>=0 for all x gives lambda>0 and discriminant<=0, so lambda*=1/3.
questions.justification: Quadratic non-negativity condition applied once, then substitution; one familiar move with short arithmetic.

questions.key_step: Both functions are strictly monotone (f increasing, g decreasing); the inequality reduces to a quadratic inequality in alpha.
questions.justification: Routine chain of standard monotonicity facts with one small justification (f'>0 for negative x); a few steps longer than 2024-P2-Q10 (L1) and similar to 2026-P2-Q3 (L2) in routine nature. Level 2.

questions.key_step: Show f is decreasing and evaluate end values, taking cot^-1(-1)=3pi/4.
questions.justification: Short chain: derivative sign, two endpoint evaluations; the only trap is the principal value of cot^-1 at -1, and options allow checking. Lighter than 2026-P1-Q1 (L3), routine multi-step. Level 2.

questions.key_step: Single critical point x=1 with f(1)<0 and f->infinity at both ends gives two roots.
questions.justification: One familiar move (root counting via the minimum value) applied once; easier than 2024-P2-Q10 (L1) only in format, same level. Level 1.

questions.key_step: f' = 7x^6+15x^2+3 > 0 and odd degree, so exactly one root.
questions.justification: Single standard trick with no computation; numerical format gives no options but the answer is immediate. Same idea as 2024-P2-Q10 (L1). Level 1.

questions.key_step: Recognise (f g')' = f g'' + f' g', count zeros of f g' using evenness, apply Rolle.
questions.justification: Needs product-derivative recognition and the less common observation that an even g gives g'(0)=0, with distractor data and no options. Two ideas linked, so Level 3, near 2023-P2-Q7 (L3).

questions.key_step: Split |2x^2+3x-2| at x=1/2; f decreasing then increasing, so min at 1/2 and max at an endpoint.
questions.justification: Routine multi-step: factor, split, differentiate, sign check, compare endpoints, simplify to option form. No insight; options help. Below 2026-P1-Q1 (L3), so Level 2.

questions.key_step: Area = 2a sin(alpha)(1-cos alpha) maximised at alpha=2pi/3, giving a=4.
questions.justification: Chain of parametrisation, optimisation, solving for a and then eccentricity; every step is standard coaching material. Routine multi-step, Level 2 (well below 2025-P2-Q8, L4).

questions.key_step: Split at the root (3-sqrt17)/2 of the quadratic inside the modulus; compare parabola vertex and end values.
questions.justification: Routine piecewise-parabola extrema with a surd root; careful but all standard, options help. Level 2, easier end of 2026-P1-Q1 (L3).

questions.key_step: Isosceles altitude AD = sqrt40 x gives area sqrt40(10x - x^3); set derivative to zero.
questions.justification: One familiar move (altitude, area, derivative) with an immediate answer; Heron's formula makes it equally quick. Level 1, like 2024-P2-Q3 (L1).

questions.key_step: Combined area is a quadratic in the triangle's wire length; find the vertex and simplify to option form.
questions.justification: Routine chain of setup, quadratic minimisation and surd simplification; no real insight but messy arithmetic, options to check against. Level 2, like 2026-P2-Q3 (L2).

questions.key_step: Sign of $f$ (or of $(x-5)^{n_2-1}$) on $(3,5)$ depends on the parity of $n_2$.
questions.justification: Single idea (parity of the exponent decides sign on (3,5)) with four short statements to read. Close to 2021-P2-Q9 (parity of exponents decides extrema) but far simpler since only one parity matters, and options allow elimination.

questions.key_step: Remove the modulus piece-wise and test the junctions $x=1,3$ as well as the interior critical point.
questions.justification: Piecewise cubic from a modulus plus junction tests; numerical answer so a slip changes the count. Comparable to 2021-P2-Q10 (count local extrema, L2) but with a modulus and two corners, so one level higher.

questions.key_step: Common normal passes through the circle's centre, giving $2t^3+3t-1=0$, then bound $x_P=1-\sin\theta$ monotonically.
questions.justification: Needs the common-normal idea, a cubic that cannot be solved exactly, and monotonic bounding to place the abscissa; long chain but options help.

questions.key_step: Implicit differentiation at $(-2,3)$ gives slope $-9/2$; intercepts give the triangle.
questions.justification: Routine chain: implicit differentiation, two lines, two intercepts, triangle area. No insight but numerical answer with arithmetic to keep exact.

questions.key_step: Solve $F_x=0$ and $F_y=0$ with the curve, and discard $y=\frac29$ since it is not on the curve.
questions.justification: Implicit differentiation with one subtle rejection (horizontal tangent), then a small elimination; no options, so slips matter.

questions.key_step: Reduce $V$ and $S$ to the single variable $h$ and chain-rule through $\frac{dh}{dt}$.
questions.justification: Three or four routine steps in one chain (geometry of cone, $dh/dt$, $dS/dt$), no insight; numerical format.

questions.key_step: Match slopes $3a^2-2a+1=22$ and then reject $a=-\frac73$ because that tangent is parallel, not identical.
questions.justification: Short chain: tangent at given point, slope equation, quadratic, rejection of the parallel case. Routine multi-step.

questions.key_step: Reduce $f'\ge0$ to $3a\le\min\frac{2}{1+4x^2}$ at $x=\pm\frac\pi6$.
questions.justification: Routine: derivative, parameter bound from an even decreasing function, substitute. Similar to 2026-P1-Q1 style monotonicity but simpler; the key conflicts with the stated function (flawed question).

questions.key_step: Continuity gives $b=-\frac14$, then $f'(x)=2x-\frac14<0$ for $x<\frac18$ disproves (C).
questions.justification: Four short statements to check on a piecewise function after finding $b$; each is routine, options allow elimination.

questions.key_step: $f'=e^{x(1-x)}(1+x-2x^2)$ and factor the quadratic.
questions.justification: One derivative, one factorisation, read the sign: a single familiar move, like standard JEE Main monotonicity.

questions.key_step: Spotting the factor (x-1)^2(x+1) in a degree-8 polynomial; the quintic factor is monotonic.
questions.justification: Needs factorising an octic by testing x=+-1 and then one monotonicity argument for the quintic, a routine chain with no options to check against. Close to 2024-P2-Q10 (L1, increasing polynomial has one root) but with an extra factoring stage, so one level higher.

questions.key_step: Finding a=1/2 from the sign change of f', then rejecting P(2,2) using the second condition.
questions.justification: Four short stages (monotonic turning point, tangent from an external point, rejection of an extraneous point, normal intercept form), each routine, with a numerical answer. Same routine-chain character as 2026-P2-Q2 (parabola tangents, L2).

questions.key_step: Noticing that y=2x+3 passes through both end points, giving four zeros, then Rolle twice.
questions.justification: One familiar idea (repeated Rolle) but the end-point observation is easy to miss, and the answer is numerical. Comparable to 2024-P2-Q10 (L1, reduce to one standard monotonicity fact) with the extra trap of counting the end points.

questions.key_step: Seeing both factors have negative derivative on [-3,0], so f decreases.
questions.justification: A short sign argument on a factored derivative with options to check against. Slightly longer than a one-trick Level 1, like 2025-P1-Q15 (L1) but needs a clean sign argument for two terms.

questions.key_step: Turning 'touches the x-axis at P' into y(-2)=0 and y'(-2)=0; solve three linear equations.
questions.justification: Three direct conditions on a cubic followed by a standard max test. No insight needed and short, with options to check against; below the routine-chain bar of Level 2 as each step is one familiar move.

questions.key_step: Comparing f(1)=3 with the right-hand limit -2+log2(b^2-4), and keeping the domain b^2>4.
questions.justification: Both branches are monotonic by a quick sign check, then a single inequality with a domain condition; options let the student sanity-check. Routine multi-step like 2026-P2-Q2 (L2).

questions.key_step: tan^{-1} is increasing so extremise sin x - cos x on [0,pi]; convert tan^{-1}sqrt2 to the cos^{-1} form.
questions.justification: One familiar move (extremise the inside of an increasing function) plus an end-point check, then a standard inverse-trig conversion to match the option. Similar in demand to 2024-P2-Q3 (L1, one familiar move) with an extra end-point check.

questions.key_step: Factor f' as k*x*(x^2-2)^2*3^{...}; read off sign, then see sign change of f'' at sqrt(2).
questions.justification: Three statements each needing a genuine check, with a long derivative whose second derivative is messy unless the factorised form is exploited; similar to the statement-checking style of 2026-P1-Q7 (L3). Options help but the work per statement is non-trivial.

questions.key_step: Splitting at x=7/5 to see the floor is constant (4) before it and both parts non-decreasing after it.
questions.justification: Needs a monotonicity split of a mixed abs + floor function and end-point checks; numerical so slips are possible but the idea is familiar. Routine chain like 2026-P2-Q2 (L2).
